messages:
incident-bot: ALERT: spike in 5xx gateway errors for private-vpc us-east-1a (routes -> inference-gw). Paging oncall. Error rate: 14% over last 5m.
Mike (oncall): I'm up — looking. Which customers impacted?
Lucas (support): Seeing increased 502/504s for customer-prod-runs. Ticket 9872 opened by CSM.
Cherise (netops): I can see a sudden increase in SYN_RECV counts on the active NAT gateway and a lot of TCP resets on the peering interface. Might be asymmetric return paths.
Tim R. (eng-runtime): Metrics: p50 latency steady but p95+ saturating, retries bumping. Runtime logs show upstream gateway timeouts and TLS resets.
SRE Pager: @Mike setting incident priority to P1. Creating incident record and zoom in 5.
Mike (oncall): Joining zoom. First steps: isolate whether this is NAT ephemeral exhaustion, SG rate limiting, or peering flaps. Cherise — can you dump conntrack summary and recent flow logs?
Cherise (netops): Running: 
```
# conntrack -S | egrep "tcp|entries" -n
entries: 65536
tcp: in_use 62100, tombstones 0
```
Looks like high usage but not full entries yet. Ephemeral port exhaustion on the gateway is possible due to bursty client connections from internal pools.
Cherise (netops): Also pulled vpc flow logs for the last 10m — high retransmit counts on peering-eni-03 and many flows marked "REJECT" from a security group we rolled out 2 days ago.
Mike (oncall): Which SG rule? Can we rollback?
Cherise (netops): Rule: sg-232 allow tcp:443 from peering-prefix but we accidentally tightened the ephemeral range to 1024-49152 -> should have been 1024-65535. Rolling back to open ephemeral ports to peering prefix now.
Tim R. (eng-runtime): While that propagates, let's fail traffic to standby NAT gateway and shift the inference-gw route to a healthy AZ. Can we initiate a graceful failover?
Cherise (netops): Initiating route reroute to standby in us-east-1b: 
```
aws ec2 replace-route --route-table-id rtb-0abc --destination-cidr-block 10.3.0.0/16 --network-interface-id eni-standby
```
Applying — ETA ~45s.
SRE Pager: Noted. Informing customers with known impact group. Lucas, can you prepare an update?
Lucas (support): Drafting: "We're investigating elevated 5xx from inference gateway in us-east-1a caused by private VPC networking anomalies. Mitigation in progress; some requests may see retries/timeouts. Will update in 15 minutes."
Mike (oncall): We should also double-check NAT conntrack eviction logs on the appliance. Cherise — any evictions?
Cherise (netops): Found logs: 
```
[WARN] conntrack: eviction triggered, high-water 90% -> dropping oldest
```
So connection shedding is happening. That explains 502s as upstream TLS handshakes fail mid-flow.
Tim R. (eng-runtime): Can runtime reduce new connection churn by enabling keep-alive pooling for inference routes temporarily? We can bump backend keepalive timeout to reduce new TCP opens.
Mike (oncall): Yes, toggle keepalive to 120s for the affected route. Tim, can you push that?
Tim R. (eng-runtime): Pushing now: 
```
PATCH /api/routes/inference-gw
{ "keepalive": 120 }
```
Pushed and confirmed by health checks.
Cherise (netops): Route replacement succeeded; peering path now via us-east-1b. Observability shows immediate drop in retransmits on the peering link.
SRE Pager: Good. Early metrics: 5xx rate down to 6% in 2m and trending down.
Mike (oncall): Keep monitoring. We'll keep SG rollback and conntrack threshold increased. Cherise, raise conntrack table size on the gateway as a stopgap.
Cherise (netops): Increasing table size and conntrack timeout for established TCP to 7200s.
Mike (oncall): Customer comms: Lucas send update noting mitigation and ETA for full recovery.
Lucas (support): Sent update to impacted accounts. CSMs acknowledge.
Tim R. (eng-runtime): I see recoveries in runtime logs — TLS handshakes success rate improving, retries back to normal.
SRE Pager: Marking incident as "mitigated" but will keep it active for postmortem. Please add notes on root cause hypothesis: SG ephemeral range misconfig + conntrack eviction causing NAT load-shedding + asymmetric peering route contributing to packet drops -> 502/504 spike.
Mike (oncall): Agreed. Assigning postmortem owners: Cherise (network root cause), Tim (runtime mitigation), Lucas (customer comms). I'll hand off to oncall-handoff channel at 3778001450.
SRE Pager: Incident updated, creating follow-up tasks: audit SG rollout process, add guardrail to prevent ephemeral-range tighten, autoscale NAT capacity and increase conntrack alert sensitivity.
Mike (oncall): Thanks team. Final status: service recovering, P1 mitigated, postmortem to follow. :thumbsup:
